name: Starling / Frank-Starling Law
def: Force of cardiac contraction is directly proportional to the initial length (end-diastolic volume) of the muscle fiber.

name: Poiseuille's Law
def: Rate of blood flow ∝ ΔP·r⁴ / (8ηL). Flow increases dramatically with vessel radius.

name: Ohm's Law
def: Blood flow = ΔPressure / Resistance. Hemodynamic analogue of electrical Ohm's Law.

name: Law of Laplace
def: Wall tension in a sphere: T = P·r / 2. Explains why small alveoli tend to collapse into large ones.

name: Landsteiner's Law
def: In ABO system, if an agglutinogen is present on the RBC, the corresponding agglutinin is absent from plasma.

name: Bell-Magendie Law
def: Dorsal spinal roots are sensory; ventral roots are motor. Established the anatomical basis of reflex arcs.

name: Einthoven's Law
def: In ECG bipolar limb leads: Lead II = Lead I + Lead III. Defines the Einthoven triangle.

name: Fick's Law of Diffusion
def: Net gas diffusion rate ∝ (surface area × ΔP) / membrane thickness. Basis of lung diffusion capacity.

name: Boyle's Law
def: At constant temperature, gas volume is inversely proportional to pressure (PV = constant).

name: Charles' Law
def: At constant pressure, gas volume is directly proportional to absolute temperature.

name: Dalton's Law
def: Total pressure of a gas mixture = sum of partial pressures of each individual gas.

name: Henry's Law
def: Amount of gas dissolved in liquid ∝ its partial pressure above the liquid.

name: Graham's Law
def: Rate of gas diffusion ∝ 1/√molecular weight. By this law O₂ (MW 32) diffuses faster than CO₂ (MW 44) in air; however, CO₂ diffuses ~20× faster than O₂ across biological membranes due to its far higher solubility (Fick's Law).

name: Avogadro's Law
def: Equal volumes of any gas at same temperature and pressure contain equal numbers of molecules.

name: All-or-None Law
def: A tissue either responds maximally to a threshold stimulus or does not respond at all. Applies to cardiac muscle and individual nerve fibers.

name: Law of the Intestine
def: Bolus of food causes contraction orad (behind) and relaxation aborad (ahead) — basis of peristalsis.

name: Weber-Fechner Law
def: Perceived sensation ∝ log(stimulus intensity). Explains why we hear in decibels.

name: Power Law (Stevens)
def: Relates actual stimulus strength to perceived signal strength by a power function (ψ = k·φⁿ).

name: Law of Projection
def: Stimulation of a sensory pathway at any point causes sensation to be referred to the original receptor location.

name: Marey's Law
def: Heart rate is inversely proportional to blood pressure (baroreceptor basis).

name: Monro-Kellie Doctrine
def: Total volume in the rigid cranium (brain + blood + CSF) is constant; increase in one must be offset by decrease in another.

name: Bernoulli Principle
def: As fluid velocity increases, its lateral pressure decreases. Explains murmurs, Venturi effect, and airway dynamics.

name: Ideal Gas Law
def: PV = nRT. Approximates gas behaviour in respiratory physiology under varying pressures and temperatures.

name: Law of Forward Conduction
def: At a chemical synapse, impulses travel only from presynaptic to postsynaptic neuron — enforces one-directional signalling.

name: Nernst Equation
def: Calculates equilibrium potential for a single ion: E = (RT/zF) × ln([X]o/[X]i).

name: Goldman-Hodgkin-Katz (GHK)
def: Calculates resting membrane potential when multiple ions (Na⁺, K⁺, Cl⁻) and their permeabilities are considered.

name: Henderson-Hasselbalch
def: pH = pKa + log([HCO₃⁻] / 0.03×PaCO₂). Used to interpret acid-base status.

name: Bohr's Equation
def: Estimates physiological dead space: Vd/Vt = (PaCO₂ − PeCO₂) / PaCO₂.

name: Bazett's Formula
def: Corrects QT interval for heart rate: QTc = QT / √RR. Normal QTc < 440 ms.

name: Radford's Formula
def: Predicts anatomical dead space (mL) ≈ 2.2 × body weight (lbs).

name: Dubois Formula
def: Calculates body surface area (m²) from height and weight; used to derive cardiac index.

name: Fick Principle
def: Cardiac output = O₂ consumption / (arterial O₂ − venous O₂). Gold-standard method for measuring cardiac output.

name: Poiseuille-Hagen Formula
def: Resistance = 8ηL / πr⁴. Relates viscosity, tube length, and radius to flow resistance.

name: Erlanger-Gasser Classification
def: Classifies nerve fibers by diameter and conduction velocity: Aα > Aβ > Aγ > Aδ > B > C.

name: Bohr Effect
def: ↑H⁺ or ↑CO₂ shifts O₂-Hb dissociation curve right → lower O₂ affinity → easier O₂ unloading in tissues.

name: Haldane Effect
def: Oxygenation of Hb in lungs displaces CO₂, doubling CO₂ release. Complement of the Bohr effect.

name: Hamburger Shift (Chloride Shift)
def: In tissues, HCO₃⁻ exits RBC in exchange for Cl⁻ to maintain electrical neutrality.

name: Gibbs-Donnan Effect
def: Asymmetric ion distribution across a membrane caused by the presence of nondiffusible charged proteins on one side.

name: Treppe (Staircase)
def: Progressive increase in contraction force during rapid, repeated stimulation of a previously resting muscle.

name: Bowditch Phenomenon
def: Increased heart rate → increased force of contraction (positive force-frequency relationship).

name: Fenn Effect
def: Muscle uses extra energy proportional to the external work it performs.

name: Post-Extrasystolic Potentiation
def: The beat after a compensatory pause (following an ectopic beat) is stronger than normal due to increased Ca²⁺ loading.

name: Post-Tetanic Potentiation
def: Twitch amplitude is increased immediately after a tetanic contraction ends.

name: Anrep Effect
def: Acute ↑ afterload → compensatory ↑ myocardial contractility. Intrinsic cardiac autoregulation.

name: Wolff-Chaikoff Effect
def: Very high iodide dose acutely inhibits thyroid hormone synthesis (organification block).

name: Jod-Basedow Phenomenon
def: Excess iodine administration triggers hyperthyroidism in a susceptible thyroid gland.

name: Aldosterone Escape
def: After 3-5 days of excess aldosterone, kidneys escape Na⁺ retention via ANP and pressure natriuresis.

name: Purkinje Shift
def: In dim light the eye shifts maximum sensitivity from ~555 nm (photopic) to ~505 nm (scotopic).

name: Lewis-Hunting Response
def: Rhythmic vasoconstriction then vasodilation during sustained cold exposure — protects against frostbite.

name: Latch-Bridge Mechanism
def: Smooth muscle cross-bridges lock in a low-energy state, sustaining tension without continued ATP hydrolysis.

name: Clasp-Knife Phenomenon
def: Sudden collapse of resistance when a spastic limb is passively stretched (Golgi tendon organ activation).

name: Windkessel Effect
def: Large elastic arteries buffer pulsatile flow from the heart into a more continuous peripheral flow.

name: Alpha Block (Arousal Response)
def: Disappearance of alpha rhythm (8-13 Hz) on EEG upon eye opening or mental effort; replaced by desynchronised beta waves.

name: Déjà Vu
def: Inappropriate sense of familiarity with a new situation; associated with temporal lobe activity.

name: Dale's Phenomenon
def: A neuron releases the same neurotransmitter(s) at all of its synaptic terminals. Basis for classifying neurons as 'cholinergic', 'dopaminergic', etc.

name: Renshaw Inhibition
def: Motor neurons activate Renshaw cells (inhibitory interneurons) that feed back to inhibit the same motor neurons.

name: P Factor (Lewis Factor)
def: Chemical substance (likely K⁺) that accumulates in ischemic muscle and stimulates nociceptors — responsible for anginal pain.

name: Place Principle
def: Different frequencies stimulate specific tonotopic locations along the basilar membrane, enabling pitch discrimination.

name: Volley Principle
def: Groups of auditory nerve fibres fire in volleys to encode high-frequency sound information beyond the limit of a single fibre.

name: Mittelschmerz
def: Brief lower abdominal pain at mid-cycle ovulation caused by minor peritoneal irritation from follicular fluid release.

name: Dumping Syndrome
def: Post-gastrectomy rapid gastric emptying → osmotic fluid shift into gut → weakness, sweating, palpitations after meals.

name: Occlusion
def: When inputs to a neuronal pool overlap, combined response is less than the arithmetic sum of individual responses.

name: Subliminal Fringe (Summation)
def: Inputs that individually fail to reach threshold can summate to produce a supramaximal combined response.

name: Bainbridge Reflex
def: Atrial wall stretch (↑venous return) → ↑heart rate via vagal inhibition and sympathetic activation.

name: Bezold-Jarisch Reflex
def: Chemical stimulation of ventricular/coronary C-fiber receptors → classic triad of bradycardia, hypotension, and apnea (followed by rapid shallow breathing). Also called coronary chemoreflex.

name: Hering-Breuer Reflex
def: Lung inflation activates pulmonary stretch receptors → inhibits further inspiration (inflation reflex).

name: Head’s Paradoxical Reflex
def: Strong lung inflation paradoxically stimulates further inspiratory effort (opposite of Hering-Breuer).

name: Cushing's Reflex
def: ↑Intracranial pressure → intense systemic hypertension + bradycardia + irregular respirations (= Cushing's triad). Driven by direct CO₂/ischaemia stimulation of the RVLM.

name: J (Juxtacapillary) Reflex
def: Pulmonary congestion stimulates J receptors → rapid shallow breathing (dyspnea).

name: Axon Reflex
def: Antidromic conduction in sensory C fibers after skin injury releases substance P → local arteriolar dilation (flare).

name: Enterogastric Reflex
def: Duodenal distension or fat/acid → inhibits gastric motility and secretion.

name: Gastrocolic Reflex
def: Stomach distension after a meal → ↑colonic motility (explains postprandial urge to defecate).

name: Micturition Reflex
def: Bladder stretch receptors → parasympathetic detrusor contraction + urethral sphincter relaxation.

name: Mass Reflex
def: After severe spinal cord injury, a minor stimulus below the lesion triggers widespread flexor spasms + bowel/bladder evacuation.

name: Vestibulo-Ocular Reflex
def: Head rotation → compensatory eye movement in the opposite direction to stabilise retinal image.

name: Accommodation Reflex
def: Near vision: lens thickens (ciliary muscle contracts), pupils constrict, eyes converge.

name: Pupillary Light Reflex
def: Light → optic nerve → pretectal nucleus → bilateral Edinger-Westphal → pupil constriction.

name: Consensual Light Reflex
def: Light in one eye → constriction of the OPPOSITE pupil (bilateral efferent limb of light reflex).

name: Tympanic (Acoustic) Reflex
def: Loud sound → contraction of stapedius and tensor tympani → stiffens ossicular chain, protects cochlea.

name: Phillipson's / Crossed Extensor Reflex
def: Noxious stimulus to one limb → flexion of that limb + extension of the contralateral limb.

name: Peristaltic (Myenteric) Reflex
def: Contraction orad + relaxation aborad to a gut bolus — the basis of normal propulsion.

name: Brown-Séquard Syndrome
def: Spinal cord hemisection: ipsilateral motor loss + fine touch/proprioception loss; contralateral pain/temperature loss.

name: Horner's Syndrome
def: Sympathetic chain damage: ptosis, miosis, anhidrosis (enophthalmos) on the ipsilateral side.

name: Klüver-Bucy Syndrome
def: Bilateral amygdala damage: hyperorality, hypersexuality, visual agnosia, fearlessness, and placidity.

name: WPW Syndrome
def: Bundle of Kent bypasses AV node → short PR, delta wave, wide QRS, risk of re-entrant tachycardia.

name: LGL Syndrome
def: Pre-excitation via James fibers: short PR interval but NORMAL QRS (unlike WPW).

name: Wenckebach (Mobitz I)
def: Progressive PR prolongation until a QRS is dropped, then cycle repeats. AV nodal block.

name: Stokes-Adams Syndrome
def: Sudden loss of consciousness due to transient complete heart block → cardiac asystole.

name: Sick Sinus Syndrome
def: SA node dysfunction → inappropriate bradycardia, sinus arrest, tachy-brady syndrome.

name: Long QT Syndrome
def: Delayed ventricular repolarisation (KVLQT1 mutation etc.) → risk of torsades de pointes and sudden death.

name: Zollinger-Ellison Syndrome
def: Gastrinoma (often in pancreas/duodenum) → massive gastrin excess → peptic ulceration + diarrhea.

name: Bartter Syndrome
def: Loss-of-function mutation in thick ascending loop transporters → hypokalemia, metabolic alkalosis, high renin/aldosterone, normotension.

name: Gitelman Syndrome
def: Like Bartter but affects DCT thiazide-sensitive transporter → also hypomagnesemia + hypocalciuria.

name: Liddle's Syndrome
def: Gain-of-function ENaC mutation → looks like hyperaldosteronism but renin and aldosterone are LOW.

name: Gordon Syndrome
def: Pseudohypoaldosteronism Type II: hyperkalemia + hypertension with normal GFR. Opposite of Bartter.

name: Fanconi Syndrome
def: Generalised proximal tubule dysfunction: glucosuria, aminoaciduria, phosphaturia, bicarbonaturia.

name: Hartnup Disease
def: Defective neutral amino acid transporter in intestine and proximal tubule → pellagra-like rash, ataxia.

name: Kallmann Syndrome
def: GnRH neuron migration failure → hypogonadotropic hypogonadism + anosmia (absent olfactory bulbs).

name: Addison's Disease
def: Primary adrenal insufficiency: fatigue, hyperpigmentation, hypotension, hyponatremia, hyperkalemia.

name: Cushing's Syndrome
def: Chronic cortisol excess: central obesity, moon face, buffalo hump, striae, hypertension.

name: Hashimoto's Disease
def: Autoimmune thyroiditis: anti-TPO antibodies destroy follicles → hypothyroidism. Most common thyroid disease.

name: Ménière's Disease
def: Endolymphatic hydrops: episodic vertigo + fluctuating sensorineural hearing loss + tinnitus + aural fullness.

name: Weber Syndrome
def: Midbrain lesion at CN III nucleus: ipsilateral CN III palsy + contralateral hemiplegia.

name: Millard-Gubler Syndrome
def: Pons lesion: ipsilateral CN VI & VII palsy + contralateral hemiplegia.

name: Avellis Syndrome
def: Paralysis of CN X (vagus) of one side (LMN type) + contralateral hemiplegia (crossed hemiplegia). Lesion in the medulla.

name: Adiposogenital (Fröhlich) Syndrome
def: Hypothalamic damage → hypogonadism + obesity. Distinct from simple obesity.

name: Lambert-Eaton Syndrome
def: Autoimmune attack on presynaptic Ca²⁺ channels at NMJ → proximal weakness that IMPROVES with repetition.

name: Guillain-Barré Syndrome
def: Acute immune demyelination of peripheral nerves → ascending flaccid paralysis, areflexia.

name: Metabolic Syndrome (Syndrome X)
def: Cluster: central obesity + insulin resistance + hypertension + dyslipidaemia + hyperglycaemia.

name: Zellweger Syndrome
def: Peroxisome biogenesis disorder: absent peroxisomes → accumulation of very-long-chain fatty acids. Neonatal.

name: Hirschsprung's Disease
def: Congenital absence of myenteric ganglion cells in colon → failure of relaxation → functional obstruction.

name: Pendred Syndrome
def: Defective thyroid organification of iodine + sensorineural deafness (pendrin mutation).

name: Monge's Disease
def: Chronic Mountain Sickness: polycythaemia, pulmonary hypertension, cor pulmonale in long-term highlanders.

name: Stein-Leventhal (PCOS)
def: Polycystic ovarian syndrome: hyperandrogenism, chronic anovulation, insulin resistance.

name: Chiari-Frommel Syndrome
def: Persistent galactorrhoea + amenorrhoea + uterine atrophy after childbirth (hyperprolactinaemia).

name: Menetrier Disease
def: Giant rugal folds + protein-losing gastropathy + increased mucus; premalignant.

name: Sjögren's Syndrome
def: Autoimmune exocrinopathy: xerostomia + xerophthalmia. Anti-Ro (SS-A) and Anti-La (SS-B) antibodies.

name: Raynaud's Disease
def: Episodic digital vasospasm in response to cold/stress → white → blue → red colour changes.

name: Buerger's Disease
def: Thromboangiitis obliterans: inflammatory arterial occlusion in young male smokers → claudication, gangrene.

name: Huntington's Disease
def: CAG repeat expansion in huntingtin gene → progressive chorea, dementia, psychiatric symptoms.

name: Tetralogy of Fallot
def: Four defects: VSD + pulmonary stenosis + overriding aorta + RVH → right-to-left shunt → cyanotic 'blue baby'.

name: Barrett's Oesophagus
def: Intestinal metaplasia of oesophageal squamous epithelium due to chronic GORD; premalignant.

name: Ebstein's Anomaly
def: Apical displacement of tricuspid valve leaflets → atrialized RV → intermittent cyanosis + arrhythmias.

name: Duchenne / Becker Muscular Dystrophy
def: X-linked dystrophin gene mutations → progressive muscle degeneration. Duchenne = absent dystrophin; Becker = reduced.

name: Whipple's Disease
def: Tropheryma whipplei infection → malabsorption, diarrhea, arthralgias, PAS-positive macrophages in lamina propria.

name: Refsum Disease
def: Phytanic acid oxidase deficiency (peroxisomal) → accumulation of phytanic acid → neuropathy, retinitis, ataxia.

name: Argyll Robertson Pupil
def: Accommodation present but light reflex absent. Seen in neurosyphilis. Mnemonic: ARP (Accommodation Reflex Present) / PRA (Pupillary Reflex Absent).

name: Adie Tonic Pupil
def: Ciliary ganglion lesion: dilated pupil with very slow (tonic) response to light and accommodation.

name: Romberg Sign
def: Loss of balance when standing with feet together and eyes closed → posterior column/proprioception lesion.

name: Babinski Sign
def: Extension (dorsiflexion) of big toe on plantar stimulation → upper motor neuron lesion.

name: Chvostek's Sign
def: Tapping facial nerve at parotid → ipsilateral facial muscle twitch; indicates hypocalcaemia.

name: Trousseau's Sign
def: Carpal spasm with BP cuff inflated above systolic for 3 minutes; indicates hypocalcaemia.

name: Corrigan's Pulse
def: Water-hammer (collapsing) pulse of aortic regurgitation — rapid upstroke and sudden collapse.

name: Cannon Wave
def: Giant 'a' wave in JVP when right atrium contracts against closed tricuspid valve (complete heart block).

name: Charcot's Triad (cerebellar)
def: Nystagmus + intention tremor + scanning speech — classic triad of cerebellar disease (e.g., MS).

name: Myerson's Sign
def: Inability to suppress blink to repeated glabellar taps — seen in Parkinson's disease.

name: Queckenstedt Test
def: During LP, compress jugular veins → CSF pressure should rise rapidly; failure suggests spinal subarachnoid block.

name: Schilling Test
def: Two-stage test: oral radioactive B₁₂ ± intrinsic factor to identify cause of B₁₂ malabsorption.

name: Hollander (Insulin) Test
def: Insulin-induced hypoglycaemia stimulates vagus → measures gastric acid output (tests vagotomy completeness).

name: Jendrassik's Maneuver
def: Patient hooks fingers and pulls apart → reinforces patellar/ankle reflexes by reducing cortical inhibition.

name: Rinne's Test
def: Tuning fork: AC > BC = normal or sensorineural; BC > AC = conductive deafness.

name: Weber's Test
def: Tuning fork on vertex: lateralises to BETTER ear in sensorineural, WORSE ear in conductive deafness.

name: Ishihara Charts
def: Pseudoisochromatic plates using coloured dots to screen for red-green colour blindness.

name: Spinnbarkeit Test
def: Measures the elasticity/stretchability of cervical mucus — peaks at ovulation due to oestrogen effect.

name: Van den Bergh Test
def: Differentiates conjugated (direct) from unconjugated (indirect) bilirubin in serum.

name: Barany's Chair
def: Rotating chair used to test semicircular canal function by inducing nystagmus.

name: Bjerrum Screen
def: Tangent screen used to map the central visual field and detect scotomas.

name: Auer Bodies
def: Abnormal azurophilic primary granules in myeloid blasts — pathognomonic of AML.

name: Howell-Jolly Bodies
def: Nuclear remnants in RBCs — seen post-splenectomy, in haemolytic anaemia, megaloblastic anaemia.

name: Arneth Count
def: Classification of neutrophils by number of nuclear lobes; left shift (fewer lobes) = immature cells; right shift = hypersegmentation.

name: Barr Body
def: Condensed inactive X chromosome visible in female cell nuclei; number = (X chromosomes − 1).

name: Snellen's Chart
def: Standardised chart of letters at distance to measure visual acuity (6/6 or 20/20 is normal).

name: Jaeger's Chart
def: Near-vision chart (J1–J7) used to assess reading vision and presbyopia.

name: Caloric Test
def: Ice water irrigation of ear canal → tests oculovestibular reflex; absent response indicates brainstem death.

name: Doll's Eyes Response
def: Passive head rotation → eyes should move opposite (brainstem intact); absent = brainstem lesion.

name: Herring Bodies
def: Axonal dilations in the posterior pituitary containing neurosecretory granules (ADH and oxytocin).

name: Kupffer Cells
def: Resident macrophages lining hepatic sinusoids — phagocytose bacteria and old RBCs.

name: Purkinje Fibers
def: Fastest conducting cells of the cardiac conduction system (2-4 m/s); also large inhibitory neurons in cerebellar cortex.

name: Renshaw Cells
def: Inhibitory glycinergic interneurons in spinal cord ventral horn — provide recurrent inhibition to motor neurons.

name: Node of Ranvier
def: Unmyelinated gap between Schwann cell segments on a myelinated axon — site of saltatory conduction.

name: Tamm-Horsfall Protein
def: Glycoprotein synthesised by thick ascending limb cells; most abundant urinary protein, forms urinary casts.

name: C-Peptide
def: By-product of proinsulin cleavage; equimolar with insulin; marker of endogenous insulin secretion.

name: K-Complexes
def: High-amplitude negative-positive EEG waves in NREM Stage 2 sleep; also triggered by external stimuli.

name: Sleep Spindles
def: Bursts of 12-14 Hz oscillations in NREM Stage 2 generated by thalamic reticular nucleus.

name: Spaces of Disse
def: Perisinusoidal spaces between hepatocytes and sinusoidal endothelium — allow exchange of proteins and lipoproteins.

name: Brunner's Glands
def: Submucosal glands in the duodenum secreting alkaline mucus to neutralise gastric acid entering the duodenum.

name: Pre-Bötzinger Complex
def: Pacemaker neuron cluster in the ventral medulla acting as the central pattern generator for respiratory rhythm.

name: Papez Circuit
def: Neural loop: hippocampus → mammillary bodies → anterior thalamus → cingulate cortex → entorhinal cortex → hippocampus. Critical for memory and emotion.

name: Kussmaul Breathing
def: Deep, rapid, laboured breathing; compensatory hyperventilation in metabolic acidosis (e.g., DKA).

name: Cheyne-Stokes Breathing
def: Waxing-and-waning tidal volume with periodic apnea; caused by delayed feedback from low cardiac output to central chemoreceptors. Seen in heart failure, bilateral cerebral hemisphere lesions, and high altitude.

name: Biot's Respiration
def: Clusters of breaths then unpredictable apnea; caused by dorsal medullary lesions or raised ICP.

name: Ondine's Curse
def: Loss of automatic respiratory drive (medullary pacemaker lesion) requiring voluntary control to breathe.

name: Apneustic Breathing
def: Prolonged inspiratory gasps with brief expiration; caused by lesion of the pneumotaxic centre in the pons.

name: Young-Helmholtz Theory
def: Trichromatic colour vision based on three cone types: L (red), M (green), S (blue). Colour blindness = missing one cone type.

name: Sliding-Filament Theory
def: Muscle contraction occurs by thin actin filaments sliding over thick myosin filaments — sarcomere shortens but filaments do not.

name: Walk-Along (Ratchet) Theory
def: Myosin cross-bridges attach, pull (powerstroke), detach, and reattach further along actin in a cyclical ratchet.

name: Traveling Wave Hypothesis
def: Sound sets up a wave along the basilar membrane; each frequency peaks at a specific location (tonotopy).

name: Milieu Intérieur
def: Claude Bernard's concept: the internal fluid environment must remain constant for cells to function optimally.

name: Hayflick Limit
def: Normal human somatic cells can divide ~50-70 times before entering senescence due to telomere shortening.
